core.title: Place every flow router artifact under the flow router home
core.given: A plan contains, or is gaining, flow router artifacts (new or existing); placement is enforced at the CONFIRM phase, so it applies from the moment the flow router is authored
core.when: The planner authors, edits or moves a flow router artifact, or brings a plan containing one to CONFIRM
core.then: Every flow router artifact lives under the flow router home.
prefer: Place flow router artifacts under the flow router home when first authoring them, rather than relocating them at CONFIRM
Ensure each flow router under the home has an entry in the registry index (registration is a required obligation of the same enforced check; see verification)
avoid: Placing flow router artifacts alongside other plan-artifact kinds or in other plan folders outside the flow router home
Leaving a flow router artifact unregistered in the registry index
core.why: Other flow router rules (registry mirroring, guards, payloads, route resolution, route-space admission) presuppose the homed and registered flow router set; an artifact outside the home or registry is invisible to them.
evidence: The confirm-phase placement check over every flow router artifact in the plan passes
On failure the finding reports the flow router's id, its path, the expected home and the actual home
verification: Presence check over every flow router plan artifact in the plan, new and pre-existing: each must lie beneath the expected flow router home; any path beneath the home, not only directly under it, satisfies placement

Registration is mandatory, not advisory: every flow router under the home must have an entry in the registry index at the profile's registry path; the realization records a proposed split into its own registration convention, which shares this check and does not remove the obligation here
The check runs at the CONFIRM phase and blocks confirmation; severity 3, strict disposition
On failure the finding reports the flow router's id, its path, the expected home and the actual home
The check does not cover plan artifacts whose kind is not flow router

values: plan artifact located under the flow router home (layout.locations#flow_router_dir)
plan artifact that is the flow router registry index (layout.registries#flow_router_registry)

fires: A plan reaches CONFIRM and contains any flow router artifact, new or pre-existing
A flow router artifact is authored, edited, moved or exists somewhere other than under the flow router home
A flow router artifact under the flow router home has no entry in the registry index
doesNotFire: A plan that contains no flow router artifacts
Plan artifacts whose subject kind is not flow router (any other plan-artifact kind) when no flow router is present

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts; the flow router home and the registry index sit beneath it
Canonical directory under the plan root that is the home of every flow router artifact; any path beneath it satisfies placement

The concrete plan-artifact kinds, including the flow router kind this rule scopes to

neutralityNotes: The convention governs plan-artifact placement, so ATDD plan vocabulary (flow router, plan, planner, the CONFIRM phase) is kept as stack-neutral methodology terminology; the artifact-kind value itself comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The only non-neutralizable content is the concrete home and registry paths, which move to profile keys (proposed layout.locations#flow_router_dir and layout.registries#flow_router_registry, no existing vocabulary key fits), and this rule's validator, template and variant ids, which stay bunOnly while core verification names the check generically. The registration half of the Bun statement is enforced, not advisory: core verification requires every homed flow router to be registered in the registry index, and the realization's splitSuggestion (planner.user-system-flow.flow-router-registered) records the intent to split it into its own convention without removing the obligation here. The path-based activation trigger is expressed as a role fact scoped strictly to the profiled flow router home and registry index, while the file_kind fact (needs_new_observer) retains content-based recognition of flow routers anywhere else in the plan.
